chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara and Ismail al-Ju'fi, that both of them asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
about what the mi'rad (blunt/crosswise arrow) kills. He said: 'There is no problem, provided it was your projectile or you made it for that purpose.'

key_terms.الْمِعْرَاضُ: Mi'rad — a blunt or headless arrow/shaft that kills by striking force rather than cutting; killing with it is disputed in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: Standard legal formula meaning 'there is no problem/objection', indicating permissibility (halal)
key_terms.مِرْمَاتَكَ: Your designated throwing/projectile weapon; the possession and intentionality condition for valid hunt

ai.seo_question: Is game killed by a blunt arrow (mi'rad) permissible to eat in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that game killed by the mi'rad — a blunt or crosswise arrow that kills by impact rather than a cutting edge — is permissible to consume, provided the mi'rad was the hunter's own designated hunting weapon. This ruling addresses a specific jurisprudential question about the conditions under which impact-killed prey is considered lawful, distinguishing between intentional use of one's own weapon versus accidental killing by another's arrow.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, and Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) both asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
about what the blunt weapon kills’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was hit by you or you made it for that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Zurarah and ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following: “Zurarah and ’Isma’il al-Ju‘fiy had asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the prey which is killed by flareless arrow. He (the Imam) said, ’It is not unlawful if it is what you have shot and it is what you have made for it.’”
